dog.description_text:
This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.

Pre-Screener Form

Mercury was surrendered to the care center as a stray, so we have no history on his behavior in a home environment. Mercury has not acclimated well to the shelter environment, and has shown highly fearful behavior during his stay. He has tolerated handling, though during his medical exam was tense, tail tucked, and whale eyeing. During his handling assessment, he was also tense and shaking, avoidant of handlers, and consistently sought exit from the room. Due to his fearful behavior, we recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide a period of decompression, any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based), and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

A volunteer writes: The shelter can be a difficult place for most dogs to feel comfortable, especially those who may not have known kindness for much of their life. When Mercury arrived, he trembled in his crate, but was tolerant of handling and leashing. A few days later, when I first meet him, he's a bit more confident and eager to leave the crate he's been housed in for over a week, though still quite timid - an air of uncertainty as he navigates this new world. He accepts pets and attention, and I'm hopeful that better days are ahead of him, as he slowly learns to find comfort in the humans entrusted with his care.

Mercury was discovered with another dog, Freddy (#267646, available via New Hope rescue), in an empty apartment in Queens. The apartment had been vacant for a few months, and no one knows who the dogs belonged to or how long they had been there. Employees of the building had been feeding and caring for the dogs for a week or so, and said they were fearful but social around people, though were reported to not get along well with one another. They were brought to the Queens ACC when no one came forward for them. The dogs each arrived with some wounds; Mercury has what appears to be a healing gash on his side, and Freddie has some wounds on her face and neck.
dog.name: Mercury
